newsitem.title: UK: Liffe white sugar ends week on quiet note.
newsitem.headline: Liffe white sugar ends week on quiet note.

text.p: White sugar futures remained very quiet throughout the late afternoon as traders prepared for the London Sugar Market annual dinner this evening.

Prices showed very little movement outside the $0.50 a tonne range they set during the morning and at the close December was trading at $317.40, up $0.70 a tonne from Thursday. Turnover totalled 495 lots.
Traders said the March/May spread had attracted some interest but otherwise activity was dull.
Technically, both the December and March contracts were following a downtrend channel starting from the reaction low on September 17.
The March channel pointed much more sharply downwards, with all of the week's highs below the 10-day moving average.
Both contracts' 14-day relative strength indices (RSIs) are hovering in oversold territory, as are the slow stochastic indicators.
Technical analysts said the whites market could be due for a bounce as the RSI was likely to correct upwards. Nearby support for December was pegged at $315.00 and resistance at $318.50.
paris whites ended with December trading at 4316.50 a tonne, down $0.10.
